What would be the approximate frequency of the heterozygote condition if this population were in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a genotype frequency table, with three columns labeled AA, Aa, and aa; the corresponding frequencies are shown as AA = 36%, Aa = 45%, aa = ?%. Then reason: The question asks for the approximate frequency of the heterozygote Aa if this population is in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, not the currently observed 45% in the table. In Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, AA = p^2. From the figure, AA = 36% = 0.36, so p = sqrt(0.36) = 0.60. Therefore q = 1 - p = 0.40. The heterozygote frequency is 2pq = 2(0.60)(0.40) = 0.48, that is, about 48%.

method.method_draft: First describe the image as a three-column genotype table with AA = 36%, Aa = 45%, and aa left as ?%. Use the displayed frequencies to infer the missing aa frequency by complement: 100% - 36% - 45% = 19%. From the question text, recognize that the desired value is the Hardy-Weinberg expected heterozygote frequency. Estimate allele frequencies from the observed genotype distribution: p for allele A is 0.36 + half of 0.45, and q for allele a is 0.19 + half of 0.45. Then calculate the Hardy-Weinberg heterozygote frequency as 2pq ≈ 0.486, giving approximately 48% to 49%, consistent with 48%.
